correctness.rationale: The normalized witness is directly verified: truthful first-round Borda scores are \((6,4,5)\), so \(B\) is eliminated and \(C\) beats \(A\); after one \(ABC\) voter reports \(BCA\), the scores become \((4,5,6)\), so \(A\) is eliminated and \(B\) beats \(C\). The frozen verifier contains two independent Baldwin winner implementations, exhaustive anonymous enumeration for every electorate size \(1\) through \(5\), and a separate labeled replay over all \(6^5\) profiles and every distinguished voter/report. A fresh independent anonymous replay reproduced zero bad profiles through four voters, exactly six at five voters, one relabeling class and labeled weight \(180\); inspection of the labeled route verifies the factor two giving \(360\) vulnerable distinguished voter-profile pairs.
correctness.risk: The theorem intentionally excludes score-tie profiles and fixed external tie-breaking.

value.rationale: Baldwin manipulation is a standard computational-social-choice problem, and the exact first tie-independent electorate where a single voter can profit gives a natural finite strategyproofness boundary. The complete orbit, prevalence and unique normalized report make this a structural classification rather than an isolated example.
value.risk: Fixed tie-breaking can change smaller-electorate behavior and lies outside the theorem.

final_claim: For tie-independent three-candidate Baldwin voting with complete strict ballots and one unilateral manipulator, no electorate of size at most four admits a profitable manipulation between unique outcomes. At five voters exactly six anonymous profiles, one candidate-relabeling orbit, are manipulable; they represent \(180\) of the \(7776\) labeled profiles and \(360\) vulnerable distinguished voter-profile pairs. After normalizing the sincere order to \(A\succ B\succ C\), the unique event is \((2ABC,1BCA,2CAB)\) with report \(BCA\), changing the winner from \(C\) to \(B\).
limitations: Exactly three candidates, strict ballots, one unilateral manipulator and unique tie-independent outcomes.
The five-voter exact prevalence is under labeled impartial-profile counting, not an empirical frequency.
